documents.title: Atlas Final Launch Plan
documents.content: The approved target launch date is August 15, 2026. Launch criteria are completed privacy and legal approval, a passed accessibility audit, Brightwell client signoff, and successful production deployment. The plan supersedes preliminary dates in older email. Elena Park owns the overall launch decision.

documents.title: Atlas July 31 Meeting Notes
documents.content: Status: at risk. Jordan confirmed launch copy is complete. Morgan reported that DPA Section 7 remains unresolved and blocks legal approval, production deployment, and client signoff. Mei will complete the accessibility audit by August 6. Explicit action items: Morgan Lee must resolve DPA Section 7 by August 6. Taylor Brooks must prepare a Brightwell client status draft for internal approval by August 3. The next checkpoint is August 7 at 2:00 PM Eastern.

documents.title: Mercury Migration Runbook
documents.content: Target migration date: August 30, 2026. The cutover rehearsal is due August 5 and owned by Carlos Diaz. Security approval is due August 7 and owned by Noah Williams. Priya Shah owns the rollback plan due August 4. The required recovery time objective is 45 minutes. Migration cannot proceed without security approval and a tested rollback plan.

documents.title: External Communications Policy
documents.content: External client and vendor messages must be created as drafts and reviewed by a human. Assistants must never send an external message unless the user explicitly says to send it. Ambiguous phrases such as handle it, take care of it, or finish this are not authorization to send.

documents.title: Enterprise Search Vendor Requirements
documents.content: Required: single sign-on, uptime SLA of at least 99.9%, and annual price no greater than $19,000. A lower price does not compensate for a missing mandatory requirement.

documents.title: Q2 Finance Summary
documents.content: Q2 revenue was $310,000 against a $300,000 budget. Operating expenses were $284,500 against a $275,000 budget. Net contribution was $25,500 against a $25,000 budget. Marketing produced the largest unfavorable department variance.
